findings.mechanism: Glyph cache (hash buckets + LRU list) fills to its configured capacity (2048 entries, ~0.7-0.8 MB of coverage bytes plus entry/malloc overhead) and then evicts the oldest entry per insert, freeing both the bitmap (raster_release) and the entry.
findings.cause: Expected warm-up: the cache is a bounded LRU, so RSS rises quickly with traffic until it is full (about 13 MB total), then stays flat. The cap is by entry count, not bytes, so a larger capacity or larger px sizes would raise the plateau.
findings.evidence: Built and ran ./textrun with 2000/20000/100000 iterations: max RSS 12932/13228/12956 KB (plateau). TEXTRUN_PROGRESS shows entries pinned at 2048 while evictions keep growing. valgrind --leak-check=full: 98,899 allocs, 98,899 frees, 0 bytes in use at exit, 0 errors. Reading cache.c: evict_oldest unlinks from the list and bucket, decrements count and bytes, frees bitmap and entry. The cache_lookup failure paths free e.
findings.discriminator: RSS and cache entries plateau at capacity while evictions keep rising, and every allocation is freed (valgrind clean). Growth stops after warm-up.
